processing: Gongfu black tea from Menghai large-leaf material: withered, rolled, fully oxidised and dried.
harvest_season: Not documented for this tea specifically; as with other Dian Hong, spring lots are generally prized.
appearance_dry: Plump strands with a dark sheen; tippy grades show golden-yellow down.
appearance_liquor: Typically a bright, deep red, as with other Dian Hong.
taste_profile: Rich aroma and a full, mellow body, in line with Dian Hong's reputation for strength and freshness.

brewing.notes: General large-leaf guidance: flash the first steeps, since long ones turn the strength rough.

vintage_note: Usually sold by harvest year and drunk within a year or two, as with other Dian Hong. Menghai is far better known for pu-erh, so check that a black tea label really states the year and category clearly.
description:
Menghai, in Xishuangbanna, is famous for pu-erh, so it surprises some drinkers that it is also one of the main Dian Hong areas. Its black tea is made from local large-leaf plants.

The method is the standard gongfu sequence, and the difference starts with the leaf. Golden down in Menghai tea tends to be a true golden yellow, compared with the chrysanthemum yellow more common in Fengqing.

Expect plump leaf, a rich aroma and a full, mellow body. Keep the steeps short, because this is strong material.

There is no protected standard for the name, and it says more about place than grade. Ask for the harvest year and picking standard, and try it next to a Fengqing Dian Hong to taste the regional difference.
history:
Black tea in Menghai goes back to the Fohai experimental tea factory, the forerunner of the Menghai Tea Factory, founded by Fan Hejun. Accounts give either 1939 or September 1940 for its founding, and one chronology places the first trial black tea in 1941. It was set up in wartime, with tea exports earning foreign currency.

Fan tried black tea from Menghai large-leaf plants there. The factory's later reputation rests mainly on pu-erh, while Menghai remains listed among Dian Hong's main producing areas.
